Define coating requirements before configuring a painting robot

Corners, recesses, rear surfaces and suspension points need explicit requirements before a robot’s spray path can be assessed.

EVS Robot Blog ↗17 September 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

Specify each surface region

EVST recommends separate coating requirements for broad surfaces, corners, recesses, rear faces and hanging points. A single description of the desired finish for the whole part can leave important areas undefined.

Motion footage does not prove coating quality

The video shows a robot approaching a suspended part, but cannot establish film thickness or coverage outside the camera’s view. Contact points with the hanging fixture may have different permitted exceptions for different products.

Separate general principles from actual settings

Spray angle and nozzle distance affect coverage, but example settings from other spraying methods should not be transferred directly to a robot. The installed nozzle and actual system must be considered.

Test the unresolved requirement

If the question concerns a deep recess, a front-face inspection will not answer it. Tests need to match the location under review and the real hanging orientation. Validating the robot path and assessing coating quality are separate steps.
